title: Bounded Critic Loop Workflow
summary: Use an independent critique and revision loop with a frozen rubric, evidence requirements, iteration budget, and human-owned acceptance decision.
prerequisites: A draft artifact and observable acceptance criteria
A versioned rubric with blocking conditions
A human owner for the final decision

sections.title: Freeze the contract before critique
paragraphs: Define purpose, audience, required and forbidden behavior, evidence, rubric anchors, blocking failures, and maximum rounds before asking for a critique. Changing the rubric after seeing a weak result turns evaluation into preference chasing.

Use a separate context, model, reviewer, or deterministic check where independence matters, but do not treat different model branding as proof of independent judgment. Give the critic the artifact and rubric, not hidden reasoning.

Worked case, supplied evidence: the incident began at 14:05 UTC after deployment 7f3a; observed errors rose from 12 to 18 per minute; the team rolled back at 14:17 UTC; errors were 13 per minute at 14:22 UTC; cause, affected customer count, and full recovery time were not supplied. The flawed draft says: "14:05 UTC: deployment 7f3a caused a 40% error increase. The issue is resolved after rollback."

Freeze this contract before critique. Purpose: produce a short factual incident-status note for support and engineering readers. The five criteria are arithmetic, source fidelity, unknowns, rendered fields, and unsupported claims. Wrong arithmetic, unsupported causation or resolution, omitted known fields, and missing UNKNOWN values are blocking. The budget is two rounds, three cumulative seconds, and four cumulative cost units. Only the human owner may accept the result.

Represent the note as structured fields before rendering prose. This lets deterministic checks compare each value with trusted evidence instead of treating keyword presence as proof. It does not establish the truth of arbitrary natural-language claims, so wording outside the structured renderer still requires human review.

Learner changed-input task, attempt this before reading the key: a separate record for incident INC-42 reports 21 errors per minute at 14:22 UTC. The trusted record reports 13 at that same time. Decide whether to replace the passing note, identify the disposition, state which version is retained, and record the human decision. Also explain what happens if the cumulative round, time, or cost budget is exhausted first.

Keep the trusted contract and evidence separate from critic and author output. A critic suggestion becomes actionable only when its criterion and evidence references match the frozen contract. Different contexts, deterministic checks, or reviewers can improve separation, but different provider branding alone does not establish independent judgment.
sections.callout: Provider-neutral transfer: the workflow can use Meta, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, Z.ai, hosted models, local models, deterministic checks, or human reviewers. Evaluate independence from context and evidence access, not brand names.

sections.title: Critique claims, revise deliberately, and stop
paragraphs: Require each finding to name the violated criterion, observable evidence, severity, and smallest useful correction. The author accepts, rejects with evidence, or escalates each finding; silently applying every suggestion can create regressions.
Rerun deterministic checks and the complete rubric after each revision. Stop at the declared round or budget limit, when no blocking finding remains, or when disagreement requires a qualified human.

The critic records F1 under arithmetic: 18 minus 12 is 6, and 6 divided by 12 is 0.5, so replace 40% with 50%. F2 records that the evidence says the incident occurred after deployment 7f3a but does not establish that the deployment caused it. F3 records that no full-recovery observation supports "resolved." F4 records that customer count was not supplied. Each finding names a frozen criterion, cited evidence field, severity, and proposed correction.

The author accepts F1 through F4. The author rejects F5, a suggestion to identify rollback as the root cause, because the supplied evidence explicitly leaves cause unknown. If reviewers disagree about recovery status, the author escalates rather than choosing a preferred claim. F1 through F4 are evidence-grounded corrections. F5 is critic invention and is not converted into evidence.

The deliberate passing revision is: "14:05 UTC: After deployment 7f3a, observed errors increased from 12 to 18 per minute, a 50% increase. The team rolled back at 14:17 UTC; errors were 13 per minute at 14:22 UTC. Cause, affected customer count, and full recovery time: UNKNOWN." The structured form used by the exercise binds every rendered value to the trusted record.
The supplied blank contract template remains available for reuse:

code.label: Critic loop contract
code.code:
Task: [ARTIFACT AND ACCEPTANCE DECISION]
Scope: [ARTIFACT, AUDIENCE, ALLOWED CHANGES, AND EXCLUSIONS]
Permissions: [WHO MAY READ, CRITIQUE, EDIT, RUN TOOLS, AND ACCEPT]
Rubric: [CRITERIA, ANCHORS, WEIGHTS, AND BLOCKING FAILURES]
Evidence: [SOURCES, TESTS, OUTPUT CONTRACT, AND USER POSTCONDITION]
Loop budget: [MAX ROUNDS, TIME, COST, AND CONTEXT]
Finding format: [CRITERION -> EVIDENCE -> SEVERITY -> PROPOSED CORRECTION]
Stop conditions: [BLOCKING RISK, LOW CONFIDENCE, CONFLICT, OR BUDGET]
Verification: [FROZEN RUBRIC, DETERMINISTIC CHECKS, REGRESSION REVIEW, HUMAN DECISION]
Recovery: [RESTORE PRIOR VERSION, PRESERVE FINDINGS, AND ESCALATE UNRESOLVED ITEMS]

sections.callout: Disposition rule: accept a grounded correction, reject an unsupported requirement with evidence, or escalate unresolved conflict. Never treat a critic claim as trusted incident evidence.

sections.title: Expected result and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the frozen contract, original artifact, reviewer configuration, criterion-linked findings, author dispositions, versioned revisions, deterministic results, round and cost record, final rubric, unresolved risks, and human decision.

Stop when the critic invents requirements, requests protected data, cannot cite observable evidence, cycles between alternatives, or exceeds budget. Restore the last passing artifact, retain the decision log, and send unresolved high-impact disagreement to a qualified human reviewer.

Save the code below as trace_replay.py and run it with Python 3. It imports only copy, json, and math from the Python standard library. The exercise uses embedded fixtures and makes no model API calls, network calls, or live source checks. The standard-library documentation is available at https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html, https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html, and https://docs.python.org/3/library/math.html.
This resource does not claim that the code was executed while drafting. The four printed lines are the exact expected output if the supplied code is run successfully.

The replay validates exact nested shapes, rejects unknown keys, and distinguishes finite numbers from booleans. Counts and observed error values must be nonnegative integers. It processes rounds in sequence, checks cumulative bounds before cycle detection, never resets a budget, detects any repeated artifact in processed history, and retains only a revision that actually passed all five criteria.

The worked-case recheck passes arithmetic because (18 - 12) / 12 equals 0.5, or 50%. Source fidelity passes because the structured identity, times, values, deployment, and relation after match the evidence. Unknowns pass because cause, affected customer count, and full recovery time are UNKNOWN. Rendered fields pass because deterministic rendering exactly matches the evidence-bound expected note. Unsupported claims pass because resolved remains UNKNOWN and no causal relation is asserted.

The changed-input task supplies 21 errors per minute for incident INC-42 at 14:22 UTC, while the trusted record supplies 13 at that same time. The result is changed-input-conflict, the actually passing v1 is retained, escalation is represented by the status, and human_decision remains UNKNOWN. The conflicting value is not silently adopted. If a cumulative budget is exceeded first, exceeded-budget takes precedence, the last actually passing revision or null is retained, and human_decision remains UNKNOWN.

Finding evidence references are criterion-specific. The source_fidelity criterion permits unknown_fields.cause because the supplied record explicitly identifies cause as unknown, and that reference supports checking whether a causal claim is being made. This does not make a cause known. F5 is still rejected because its proposed root-cause statement is unsupported. An unrelated or otherwise invalid reference still fails the arbitrary-reference check.

Expected output is exactly four lines: "PASS baseline rubric: 5/5", "PASS changed input: conflict, retained v1, human decision UNKNOWN", "PASS 8 deterministic failure cases", and "PASS 6 malformed shape cases". Assertions cover a good-to-bad regression, an invented criterion, missing evidence, disagreement, cumulative budget excess, a repeated-history cycle, a changed rubric, malformed input, retained-version behavior, all five separately evaluated rubric results, the accepted and rejected worked-case findings, and an invalid evidence reference.

Deterministic checks can establish agreement with this frozen structured fixture. References, disposition text, and rendered-field equality cannot prove that unrestricted free-text critique or prose is true. A human must evaluate the justification and make the final acceptance decision.

These workflow principles are consistent with first-party evaluation guidance from OpenAI at https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evaluation-best-practices, Anthropic at https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests, and Google at https://ai.google.dev/responsible/docs/evaluation. Those sources concern evaluation practices. They do not independently establish the incident facts, which are supplied fixtures for this exercise.
